title: Your mail gateway's blocklist check can fail open or fail closed without logging anything. It depends on your DNS resolver
content_md:
Most mail gateways and spam filters check sender IPs against DNS blocklists (Spamhaus ZEN, SpamCop, Barracuda). The lookup is plain DNS, so it goes through whatever resolver the box is using. That makes it a security control that can switch itself off, or start blocking everything, with nothing in the logs. Spamhaus refuses to answer queries that come through big public resolvers. Ask it about its own test entry, which RFC 5782 says is always listed: dig +short 2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org @8.8.8.8 (empty) dig +short 2.0.0.127.zen.spamhaus.org @1.1.1.1 127.255.255.254 A working resolver returns 127.0.0.2 .
